title: Cloze test: a morning at the border post
text:
Read the passage and choose the most appropriate word for each numbered blank.

Every morning the jawans at the border post (1) ........ up before sunrise. After a short prayer, they go out (2) ........ patrol in small groups. The path is narrow and rocky, so they walk slowly and look out (3) ........ any movement. By noon they return to the post. They are tired, (4) ........ they are still cheerful. In the evening they write letters to their families, who are (5) ........ of them.

title: Reading comprehension: the village library
text:
When Meena returned to her village after college, she found that the children had almost no books to read outside their school texts. She collected old books from friends in the city and set up a small library in one room of the panchayat building.

At first only a few children came, and most of them only looked at the pictures. Meena began reading stories aloud every Sunday. Within a year, more than sixty children were borrowing books regularly, and some parents had started coming to read newspapers. The room that had once stored broken furniture had become the busiest place in the village.

title: Cloze test: planting trees
text:
Read the passage and choose the most appropriate word for each numbered blank.

Last monsoon, the students of our school decided to plant trees (1) ........ the playground. Each class was given ten saplings to look (2) ........ . The students watered them every day and put small fences around them (3) ........ goats would not eat the leaves. Today most of the saplings are taller (4) ........ the students who planted them. The school now plans to plant more trees (5) ........ year.

title: Reading comprehension: the honest porter
text:
Ramesh worked as a porter at a busy railway station. One evening, after a crowded train had left, he found a leather bag lying on the platform. Inside were some clothes, a few books and an envelope full of money.

Ramesh could easily have kept the bag, but he took it straight to the station master. The next morning a worried teacher came looking for it; the money was meant for his daughter's college fees. He tried to give Ramesh a reward, but Ramesh politely refused. 'I only did my duty,' he said. The station master later praised him in front of all the staff.
